  Special City Council Meeting

To protect public health, this meeting is being held in accordance with AB 361, Government
Code section 54954(e)(1) (A). Given the proclaimed state of emergency and the Los Angeles
County Health Department recommendation for social distancing for public meetings, which is
also consistent with Cal OSHA requirements for social distancing, the City will be conducting
public meeting via video/teleconferencing and there will be no physical location available for
this meeting.  To participate in the City of Commerce ‘public meetings and provide public
comment during the COVID-19 public health emergency, please follow these steps:

1. Watch or Listen: Meetings are broadcast/streamed live on the City of Commerce’s
Facebook:  https://www.facebook.com/City-of-Commerce-123903054365151/?ref.  Archived,
on-demand video of each meeting is maintained on the City’s Facebook as part of the public
record.

2. Submit Comments before the Meeting: Members of the public can provide public comment
by sending an e-mail to cityclerk@ci.commerce.ca.us for City Council meetings, and the
comment will be read during Public Comment portion.

3. Live Remote Public Comments: Members of the public may submit live public comment via
Zoom conferencing by using the link below. You must download the Zoom app or software.
Zoom meetings can be accessed by telephone, computer, or smart device. You will be allowed

AGENDA ITEMS AND ACTIONS
5:00 P.M. CLOSED SESSION

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Rebollo called meeting to order at 5:07 p.m. via teleconferencing

ROLL CALL

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION ITEMS Administrative Services Director and City Clerk Shumway read a comment submitted by Jason Stinnett thanking outgoing councilmembers and welcoming newly-elected councilmembers.  

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION City Council/Successor Agency recessed to Closed Session at 5:11 p.m.

RECONVENE TO OPEN SESSION City Council/Successor Agency reconvened to Open Session at 6:25 p.m.

ORAL CLOSED SESSION ANNOUNCEMENT City Attorney Tapia reported on Closed Session items:

Items #1 and #3.B were not discussed in the Closed Session.

Items #2, #3.A, #4 and #5 - staff made the presentation, feedback was provided and no reportable action was taken on any of these items.  

6:00 P.M. - CITY COUNCIL MEETING

CALL TO ORDER Mayor Rebollo called regular City Council meeting to order at 6:27 p.m. via teleconferencing.  

ROLL CALL

APPEARANCES AND PRESENTATIONS

1.. Presentation/Update from the Sheriff's Department Regarding Public Safety in the City of Commerce There was no presentation from the Sheriff's Department. 

2.. A Resolution Declaring the Month of July 2022 as Parks & Recreation Month Parks and Recreation Director Alaniz spoke about parks programs. There was a video highlighting different activities over the past year. Councilmembers and the Mayor complimented parks and recreation staff for their outstanding work, including the recent Fourth of July celebration. 

Councilmember Garcia requested that all sports programs are brought back as before the pandemic. 

Vice Mayor Argumedo moved, seconded by Mayor Rebollo, to approve a Resolution declaring the month of July 2022 as Parks and Recreation Month. The motion was carried by the following vote: 

AYES: Councilmembers Altamirano, Garcia, Lainez, Vice Mayor Argumedo and Mayor Rebollo (5)


PUBLIC COMMENT There were no individuals wishing to address the City Council on any items within their jurisdiction. 




CONSENT CALENDAR  -  Action: adopt (Pass) Moved by Kevin Lainez

7.. Agreement with Robert Half International Inc for Professional Accounting Services and Bank Reconciliation Support Services

8.. Street Lighting Improvements on Eastern Avenue from Steven’s Steakhouse to Jillson Street

9.. Purchase of One (1) Toyota Forklift Model 50-8FGU25 From Atlas Toyota Material Handling

10.. Second Amendment to the Professional Service Agreement with Stantec Architecture Incorporated for Architecture and Engineering Services

4.. Re-Ratifying the Proclamation of a State of Emergency by Governor Newsom, and Re-Authorizing Remote Teleconference Meetings of the Legislative Bodies of the City of Commerce for the 30-Day Period

5.. Letter of Opposition to AB 1186 (Wiener) Medicinal Cannabis Patients Right of Access Act

6.. Letter of Opposition to SB 972 (Gonzalez) Sidewalk Food Vending

11.. Professional Services Agreement to RJM Design Group, Inc. for the City of Commerce Park and Open Space Master Plan

3.. Approval of Warrant Register Nos. 22A, 22B and 22C

SCHEDULED MATTERS

12.. Appeal of Traffic Commission Denial of Disabled Blue Curb Parking Request at 2241 Strong Avenue Acting Public Works Director Nila provided an overview of the staff report. 

Discussion took place about the on-site parking and not enough room for exit vehicles and enter the home, and whether there is a consideration for dimensions of the on-site parking. Acting Director Niles stated that it is not taken into account. In addition, the applicant could not join the meeting, and there was a consensus to table this item for the next meeting and may give the applicant the opportunity to collect two additional signatures of the neighboring properties.

CITY COUNCIL/SUCCESSOR AGENCY REPORTS Councilmember Garcia requested an agenda item to bring all sports programs back, including a review of the budget and schedules. 

Councilmember Lainez and Altamirano expressed their excitement to work with the new Council. 

Councilmember Argumedo thanked outgoing Councilmembers and his wife for supporting him through his tenure as a Councilmember and elections. 

Mayor Rebollo requested an agenda item to see if a similar meeting outside as a swearing-in ceremony meeting could be arranged in every park at least once a year if weather permits to engage the community. 


ADJOURNMENT Adjourned at memory of Rosalina Lopez at 7:12 p.m.
